A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite additions, reorganization, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original VGG10/CIFAR-10 and MLP/FashionMNIST experiments, including training dynamics, misclassified-sample analyses, and appendix correlation studies.

after.justification: v3 reports original training-dynamics and correlation results for VGG-11, MLP, and LeNet, including evaluations of network-wide sensitivity and sharpness measures.

M1.justification: Both versions analyze conventional SGD-trained feedforward networks under quadratic loss. The additions concern diagnostic metrics and mathematical bounds, without introducing or revising a training or inference algorithm.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST classification remain the evaluated coverage, including training, test, and misclassified samples. LeNet uses existing CIFAR-10 coverage. The OOD and language-model examples added in Section 4.1 are discussion, not new experiments.

E2.justification: Petzka et al.'s relative flatness becomes an evaluated comparator in v3 Figures E.5–E.7; it was absent from v2's correlation comparisons. Those comparisons also drop G, and the MLP matrix drops intermediate bound C, although C remains in the bound-tightness analysis.

E3.justification: v3 replaces G with MLS in dynamics plots, replaces test loss with generalization gap in correlation matrices, and adds NMLS and its bound. Correlation cohorts increase from 20 to 100 networks, and LeNet is added. Figures 1–2 extend to 500,000 iterations versus 150,000 and 100,000 in v2. VGG10 becomes VGG-11 in the reported configuration, although the PDFs do not establish whether that naming change reflects an architectural change.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends the correlation analyses to examine whether the all-layer bound avoids inconsistent correlations found for the input-layer bound, and whether relative flatness tracks generalization across VGG, MLP, and LeNet. The original bound-tightness plot is retained as Figure E.4, corresponding to v2 Figure D.4, rather than being a new analysis.

E5.justification: The main experiments still report five random initializations per learning-rate/batch-size setting. Pearson-correlation reporting remains unchanged, without added confidence intervals or significance tests. The 20-to-100 increase concerns the heterogeneous correlation cohort, not a stated increase in seed replicates at fixed settings.

E6.justification: The MLP MLS–D correlation changes from -0.93 in v2 Figure D.6 to -0.60 in v3 Figure E.6 for the expanded cohort. Newly reported NMLS–bound correlations are 0.92, 0.68, and 0.64 for VGG-11, MLP, and LeNet. v3 also adds relative-flatness results and revises numerous curves and matrix entries. These are revised or additional results under changed settings, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 strengthens the mixed-norm inequality in Equation (5), revises the volumetric bound in Equation (12), and introduces network volumetric ratio and NMLS bounds in Equations (13) and (15). Appendices B–C expand their derivations, and new Appendix D connects the analysis to normalized sharpness. Equation (15) omits the input's layer index used in Appendix C Equation (29), leaving a formula inconsistency.

C1.justification: v2's contribution list claims reparametrization-invariant bounds. v3 withdraws that claim and makes the consistent positive correlations obtained using the all-linear-weight bound a central contribution. The broader connection between flatness and representation compression, and the distinction from local dimensionality, remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges the bounds' lack of strict reparametrization invariance and interprets normalized sharpness through robustness to internal representations. Section 4.1 adds substantive reasons why input robustness need not benefit OOD or instruction-sensitive tasks. Section 3.2 also replaces v2's assertion of poor volume–sharpness correlation with reasonable but imperfect correlation.

D1.justification: New Appendix G states that all experiments can run on one NVIDIA Quadro RTX 6000 GPU. v2 contains no corresponding hardware disclosure; this adds resource information without establishing a change in experimental hardware.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands its relationship to normalized and reparametrization-invariant sharpness through Tsuzuku et al. and Petzka et al., including analytical and empirical connections. It removes the information-bottleneck discussion and several simplified-linear-model references, while adding OOD-generalization context and dataset citations.

P1.justification: Language edits concentrate on the abstract, introduction, terminology, and explanatory transitions. The five main sections and much of the exposition remain. Prior-work discussion is redistributed, Sections 3.4 and 4.4 are added, and appendices are reorganized around the expanded analysis.

P2.justification: The six-variable VGG and eight-variable MLP correlation matrices become nine-variable matrices, with an additional nine-variable LeNet figure. Dynamics plots are redrawn with MLS and revised axes and legends. Title styling, headings, citation colors, and page layout also change; several appendix figures are retained but relocated or modified.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects v2's central invariance overclaim and derives and tests an all-layer alternative to the problematic input-layer bound. The expanded correlation analyses and clearer applicability qualifications substantially strengthen the paper's central theoretical and empirical argument. The Equation (15)/Appendix C inconsistency and limited implementation detail temper precision, but do not outweigh these gains.
